module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 2

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/2](https://www.erdosproblems.com/2)

Erdős asked whether the smallest modulus in a distinct covering system can be arbitrarily large.
Hough proved that the answer is no, and Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba later
gave a simpler proof with an improved explicit upper bound.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos2

/--
Can the smallest modulus of a covering system be arbitrarily large?

This problem has a negative answer: there is a universal bound on the least modulus of any
distinct covering system.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_2 :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, ∀ i, ∃ m : ℕ,
        c.moduli i = Ideal.span {(m : ℤ)} ∧ B < m := by
  sorry

end Erdos2

reformulations.difference: The source uses finite distinct congruence classes with numerical moduli and asks whether their least modulus can be arbitrarily large. Lean uses ideal-valued moduli in StrictCoveringSystem ℤ and asks for natural generators exceeding each bound B.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every nonzero proper ideal of ℤ has a unique natural generator m ≥ 2. Equality of these ideals is equivalent to equality of their natural generators, and membership in a + (m) is congruence to a modulo m. StrictCoveringSystem supplies finiteness, distinct moduli, and coverage; coverage also forces the index type to be nonempty. Thus requiring every generator to exceed B is equivalent to the least modulus exceeding B. Quantifying over all natural B expresses arbitrary largeness, and answer(False) correctly denies it. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved equivalence with the numerical-congruence formulation and with existence of a uniform upper bound, without using the problem theorem or sorry axioms.

sources_consulted: Bob Hough, Solution of the minimum modulus problem for covering systems, Introduction and Theorem 1, Annals of Mathematics 181 (2015), 361–382. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1307.0874v3

Paul Balister, Béla Bollobás, Robert Morris, Julian Sahasrabudhe, and Marius Tiba, On the Erdős Covering Problem: the density of the uncovered set, Introduction and section The Minimum Modulus Problem. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1811.03547
Local Mathlib sources: RingTheory/Ideal/Span.lean, RingTheory/Ideal/Norm/AbsNorm.lean, RingTheory/Ideal/Int.lean, Data/Int/ModEq.lean, and Algebra/Group/Pointwise/Set/Basic.lean.
review.notes: The sole theorem and both docstrings agree with the primary literature: Hough resolved the problem negatively, and Balister–Bollobás–Morris–Sahasrabudhe–Tiba give a simpler proof and improved bound. Lean boundary checks excluded empty index types and generators 0 or 1, and constructed a genuine distinct covering satisfying the existential for B = 0 and B = 1.
